oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Hermeneutic Virtue: From the Common to the Fecund
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Risser, James
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: Gadamer
hermeneutic virtue
friendship
Aristotle
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Primarily in his work after Truth and Method, Gadamer emphasizes the need for understanding through practical reasoning (phronesis) as a way of meeting the challenge in living together in a world dominated by science and technology. In a 1994 essay Gadamer explicitly identifies this need for understanding as a matter of acquiring “hermeneutic virtue,” suggesting that the issue involves more than the employment of an alternative form of reasoning. This paper demonstrates just how Gadamer’s use of the phrase “hermeneutic virtue” conveys an expansion of the character of understanding in the context of social life. Hermeneutic virtue includes not only Aristotle’s modification of phronesis through the concepts of sunesis, gnome, and sungnome, but also the implicit bond of communality that Gadamer identifies with the Aristotelean virtue of friendship. In Gadamer’s reframing of friendship for the life of understanding in social life, it can be shown that such understanding is not only a way of countering the struggle for recognition with its inherent inequality but also a way in which life opens unto its fecundity.
oai_dc:dc.dc:source: Journal of Gadamer Studies; Vol. 1 No. 2 (2026): Language, Virtue, Friendship and Communal Practice
